question: Why does calling s.area() run Circle's implementation, even though s is declared with the type Shape?
options: Because Java ignores declared types entirely
Because interfaces automatically inline their implementing class's code at compile time
Because Java uses the object's actual runtime type (Circle) to resolve the overridden method call — this is runtime polymorphism
explanation: Even though the reference type is the interface Shape, the JVM dispatches the call based on the object's actual runtime class, Circle — this dynamic dispatch is how polymorphism works in Java.
